player.name: Maren Holloway
player.concept: a methodical human investigator, patient and kind, who writes everything down

established: Cob claims the boots are his and says he found them.
The left boot crackles when Cob stamps.

Sewn into the lining of Prout's left boot was a page razored from the Royal Granary Roll: a dozen grain wagons for the King's Road this past month marked 'lost to goblins', each countersigned 'J. Sallow, for the Royal Purveyor', with Prout's pencilled note beside each of what the same wagon weighed at the river warehouses two days later, and at the foot: 'Not goblins. Who pays the hedge-folk?'
Cob lets Maren read the folded page sewn into Prout's left boot, which remains Cob's.
Moll has moved between Maren and Cob and is urging Cob toward the gate.
Moll says she does not know whether the bandaged-hand man will return
Kell agrees to keep Cob and Moll nearby.
Moll tells Maren about the loose board behind the water butt and Cob's nest in the loft.

opened.title: J. Sallow and the Purveyor's office

rulings.act: ask Moll for her name and the gentleman's description and direction
rulings.why: either way it comes to the same
rulings.changed: Moll says, “Moll. Good coat, silver-topped cane, wheat-ear ring, and enough lavender water to choke a horse. His big friend had a bandaged hand and called him ‘Master Sallow.’ He went out through the gate.”; came out: silvertop

rulings.act: Ask Cob about his boots and whether he saw the gentleman
rulings.changed: Cob scowls and says, “Found ’em. They’re Cob’s, and no, Cob didn’t see nobody this morning.” He stamps once; the left boot crackles. Moll snaps, “Shut it, Cob,” and watches the gate

rulings.act: Ask Cob to let you read what's in his left boot
rulings.changed: Cob watches you for a long moment, then scowls and holds out his left boot. “Look, then. And Cob’s having it straight back.” In the lining, you find a folded page sewn in with small, neat stitches; it lists grain wagons marked “lost to goblins,” each countersigned “J. Sallow, for the Royal Purveyor.”; the scene went to What Prout found; came out: page

rulings.act: Ask Cob whether Prout gave him the boots and when he last saw him alive
rulings.changed: Cob snatches the boot back and turns his shoulder to you. “Cob told you, they’re Cob’s. Quit poking at it.” Moll drops from the wall and moves between you and Cob, watching the gate as she urges him toward it

rulings.act: Ask Moll whether the gentleman's companion is coming back
rulings.why: it comes freely when asked (dangerous, plausible, hostile)
rulings.changed: Moll answers, flatly, “I don’t know. He left with Master Sallow.” At the mention of Sallow, Cob goes white and grips the boot tighter; Kell quietly adds Moll’s answer to her notes

rulings.act: Ask Kell to keep the children nearby and inspect the granary exterior
rulings.changed: Kell answers, “I’ll keep them here.” She stays with Cob and Moll while you walk the granary’s exterior. The swept yard and the rain leave no useful trail, and you find no other ground door, stair or reachable window into the loft; the barred loft door remains the only apparent access

rulings.act: Ask Moll for a hidden way into the loft and where Sallow hides
rulings.changed: Moll studies you, then answers in a low voice: “There’s a loose board behind the water butt. Cob sleeps up there.” She glances toward the gate. “As for Sallow, I don’t know where he goes.”
